milestone: Brownie MCP Runtime Safety Policy Finite Closure

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Requires MCP tools/call input and successful structured output to satisfy task-pinned bounded schema contracts without widening policy.
Prevents autonomous runs from treating malformed or drifting MCP data as completed-success replay evidence.
Keeps MCP tool data crossing runtime boundaries schema-checked and bounded below Mode Pack policy, annotations, approval binding, and catalog provenance.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances runtime_permission_enforcement and headless_autonomous_development while preserving controlled_workspace_tools boundaries.
answers.new_capability: Runtime validates MCP tools/call input before server execution and validates successful structured output before ToolExecutionCompleted or success replay evidence.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: MCP-S4 bound approval-required calls, but arguments were still only object-checked and successful structured output was not validated against a bounded schema subset.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: MCP schemas would remain fingerprinted provenance only, allowing malformed inputs or schema-incompatible successful outputs to cross runtime evidence boundaries.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase changes Runtime MCP catalog admission, pre-call validation, success evidence, replay safety, specs, and audits; it is not a wrapper, adapter manifest, transport expansion, or documentation-only verdict.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume paths are preserved; schema validation is Runtime-owned execution gating.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase updates existing execution behavior and evidence rather than adding a summary endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Invalid or unsupported MCP schemas fail closed at catalog admission, invalid input denies before tools/call, and invalid successful structured output becomes ToolExecutionFailed rather than ToolExecutionCompleted.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Autonomous runs cannot replay or continue from MCP success evidence unless schema validation succeeded or no output schema applies.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes MCP-S5 and leaves MCP-S6 through MCP-S7 open before Runtime Release Ready.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: MCP-S5 changes Runtime MCP schema admission and execution evidence, so strict review must verify schemas fail closed, remain non-authoritative, and cannot bypass Mode Pack policy, annotations, approval binding, or catalog drift.

exit_criteria: MCP catalog admission validates inputSchema and optional outputSchema against a bounded Runtime-owned JSON Schema subset.
Known unsupported schema validation keywords fail closed instead of being ignored.
MCP tools/call input is validated before server execution and invalid input does not launch tools/call.
Successful structured output is validated before ToolExecutionCompleted and completed-success replay evidence.
Schema validation cannot override Mode Pack allow-lists, mcp_tool_access, S2 safety policy, S3 annotations, S4 approval binding, or catalog drift.
Raw schemas, raw inputs, raw MCP responses, absolute paths, environment values, and secrets are not persisted.
MCP-S5 is marked closed while MCP-S6 through MCP-S7 and Runtime Release Ready remain open.
behavior_evidence: brownie-runtime focused test coverage proves invalid MCP input is denied before tools/call and valid input records bounded schema validation evidence.
brownie-runtime focused test coverage proves unsupported schema keywords fail closed at catalog admission.
brownie-runtime focused test coverage proves invalid successful structured output is Failed rather than Completed and omitted outputSchema preserves existing success behavior.
docs/architecture/mcp-runtime-safety-policy-audit.json records MCP-S5 as closed while leaving MCP-S6 through MCP-S7 open.

accepted_capability: MCP tool input and output schema enforcement is Runtime-owned and bounded.
Schema-compatible MCP execution remains task-pinned, provenance-bound, and replay-safe without raw schema/input/response ledgering.
behavior_evidence: Runtime focused MCP schema-validation test coverage proves input denial before tools/call, output validation before success evidence, unsupported keyword fail-closed behavior, and omitted outputSchema compatibility.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the execution, admission, replay, permission, tool, workspace mutation, and completion authority.
Mode Pack structured policy remains the MCP tool safety authority; MCP schemas, annotations, descriptions, results, and model output cannot grant authority.
Schema validation only rejects or validates data at runtime boundaries; it cannot widen Mode Pack policy, allow-list membership, approval binding, annotations, or catalog provenance.
non_goals: Does not add a Brownie-specific tool adapter SDK or protocol.

Does not add Streamable HTTP, OAuth, MCP Apps, Sampling, Roots, Elicitation, public registry, automatic install, scheduler, daemon, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, or recursive Brownie invocation.
Does not close MCP-S6 or MCP-S7.
Does not close full CI workflow hardening while workflow update authority is unavailable.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected full JSON Schema support because unsupported semantics must fail closed in v0 rather than be partly interpreted.
Rejected schema-derived permissions because schemas are data contracts, not authority.
Rejected ledgering raw schemas, inputs, or MCP responses because fingerprints and bounded validation metadata are sufficient evidence.
technical_debt: MCP-S6 secret reference contract remains open.
Previously recorded Runtime Release Readiness blockers remain open, including full CI workflow hardening.

runtime_release_dod: Runtime-owned MCP permission checks, tool execution, bounded evidence, replay, and completion semantics.
Task-pinned Mode Pack policy, catalog provenance, annotation provenance, approval provenance, and point-of-use Runtime safety enforcement.
runtime_boundary_contracts: Existing tool.execute, task.run, and headless run/resume paths.
Existing ToolExecutionCompleted, ToolExecutionFailed, ToolExecutionDenied, and MCP approval ledger evidence.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: Scheduling, background polling, daemonization, hosted queues, worker fleets, and remote server operations.
external_adapter_responsibilities: MCP server implementation, GitHub/GitLab/Slack adapters, OAuth application wiring, and remote transport hosting.
commercial_solution_readiness: Enterprise tenant management, SSO/RBAC server, admin UI, monitoring backend, billing, SLA, private registry, and certified stack.

next_capability_rationale: MCP-S6 should add a Runtime-owned secret reference contract for scoped ephemeral MCP child environment injection without persisting secret values.
